# SurfaceOne — setup

Add SurfaceOne to an Angular 22 application in three steps.

## 1. Install the packages

```bash
npm install @surface-one/angular @surface-one/tokens
```

The markdown entry point also needs its optional peers (`marked`, `dompurify` and the `@codemirror/*` packages). Install them only if you import `@surface-one/angular/markdown`.

## 2. Load the styles

Add the tokens and the component stylesheet to the `styles` array of your build target, tokens first:

```json
"styles": [
  "@surface-one/tokens",
  "@surface-one/angular/styles.css",
  "src/styles.css"
]
```

Component styles are global on purpose: most parts are projected or portaled, where emulated encapsulation cannot reach.

## 3. Enable localization

Components mark their built-in strings (such as “Close”) with `$localize`, so add the polyfill:

```bash
ng add @angular/localize
```

## Use a component

```ts
import { Component } from "@angular/core";
import { SoneButtonDirective } from "@surface-one/angular/button";
import { SoneSwitchComponent } from "@surface-one/angular/switch";

@Component({
  selector: "app-root",
  imports: [SoneButtonDirective, SoneSwitchComponent],
  template: `
    <sone-switch [(checked)]="enabled" ariaLabel="Notifications" />
    <button soneBtn variant="outline" type="button">Save</button>
  `,
})
export class App {
  enabled = true;
}
```

Next, pick a skin and colour mode on the [Theme](/theme) page.
